_note: Narrative for the ISA/IEC 62443-4-1 Secure Product Development Lifecycle assessment. Boilerplate inserted VERBATIM; the executive summary is composed by slot-substitution only (no free-writing). The instrument framing supplies the 'About this assessment' prose; this pack adds the composed executive summary, a caveat box and the consultant blocks. Aim: an achieved-maturity PROFILE across the eight practices - never a single grade - with not-met and lowest-maturity requirements surfaced as floor findings. NOTE the audience: 4-1 assesses a PRODUCT SUPPLIER's development process, not an asset owner's environment, so the stakes are expressed as what ships to the asset owners who deploy the product.

boilerplate.report_intro: This report presents a maturity assessment of the organisation's secure product development lifecycle against ISA/IEC 62443-4-1. It gives the maturity each requirement achieved in the eight practices and sets out a prioritised roadmap for the requirements that are not met or are at the lowest maturity. The assessment covers the development process behind a product. The security capabilities of an individual product are covered by the companion part, 62443-4-2, and the environment where the product is installed is out of scope.
boilerplate.not_certification_caveat: This is a maturity assessment of the secure product development lifecycle against ISA/IEC 62443-4-1. The consultant placed each requirement at one maturity level using the ML anchors. The results form an achieved-maturity profile across the eight practices, with no single grade. The assessment does not certify the organisation or its products, and it does not state conformance with the standard. Mean maturity is shown for context only. The achieved maturity reflects what could be demonstrated at the time of the engagement and should be confirmed during remediation.
boilerplate.series_context: ISA/IEC 62443 is a series of standards, divided according to who is responsible for what. This part, 62443-4-1, deals with the product supplier and the development process behind a product. The assessment rates how well established each practice is. Its companion 62443-4-2 covers the security capabilities of the product itself, and the 3-x parts address the system built from those products.

executiveSummary._note: Composed by slot-substitution only; boilerplate VERBATIM; consultant blocks seeded with data-derived facts plus a marked placeholder. No free-writing. Order: verdict, scope + profile, gap-shape, profile-method + stakes, path forward + confidence. Works with or without the optional target-ML overlay.

templates.exec_verdict: This assessment maps the maturity of {clientName}'s secure product development lifecycle against ISA/IEC 62443-4-1. Of the eight practices, maturity is lowest in {weakestElementName}. The roadmap in this report concentrates on the requirements that are not met or are at the lowest maturity.
templates.exec_verdict_nogaps: This assessment maps the maturity of {clientName}'s secure product development lifecycle against ISA/IEC 62443-4-1 and sets out the achieved-maturity profile across the eight practices. Every requirement is met at some level.
templates.exec_scope: The assessment covered {answeredCount} applicable requirements across {elementCount} practices{notMetClause}.
templates.exec_profile: The achieved-maturity profile is {ml1} at ML1, {ml2} at ML2, {ml3} at ML3 and {ml4} at ML4, with {notMet} not met.
templates.exec_profile_targets: Against the target maturity, {meeting} of {compared} assessed requirements meet their target and {below} fall short.
templates.exec_gap_shape: {gapConcentrationSentence} Maturity is uneven across the lifecycle, and the weakest practice is {weakestElementName}{weakestDetail}.
templates.exec_path_forward: The roadmap in this report deals first with the requirements that are not met, then raises maturity where it most affects what reaches the customer.
templates.exec_confidence: These findings are based on the {coveragePct} of applicable requirements that could be assessed ({confidenceLabel}). Mean maturity is shown for context only. A not-met requirement is reported separately as a floor finding, so the mean cannot hide it.

gapConcentrationFragments.notMet: {notMet} requirement(s) are not met, so parts of the lifecycle are not performed at all.
gapConcentrationFragments.lowMaturity: Maturity clusters at the lower levels in {lowMaturityList}.

boilerplate.exec_profile_method: ISA/IEC 62443-4-1 assesses each requirement independently at one maturity level (ML1 Initial, ML2 Managed, ML3 Defined / Practiced, ML4 Improving). The results form a maturity profile with no single grade, because a development organisation can be strong in one practice and weak in another. An average would hide the gaps that most need attention, so the roadmap is built from specific requirements.
boilerplate.stakes: Maturity describes how reliably a development practice is performed. ML1 is ad hoc, ML2 is documented and repeatable, ML3 is actively practised on every release, and ML4 is measured and improving. A requirement that is Not met is not performed at any level. Weaknesses in the lifecycle are shipped to customers inside the product. Unmet requirements in specification, design or verification let exploitable weaknesses reach the asset owners who deploy the product. A customer or certification body assessing against 62443-4-1 would look at these first.
boilerplate.not_determination: This is a maturity assessment of the secure product development lifecycle against ISA/IEC 62443-4-1, set by the consultant against the ML anchors. It does not certify the development process, and it does not by itself establish conformance with the standard. The achieved maturity reflects what could be demonstrated during the engagement and should be confirmed during remediation.
